description: This hearty Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a beloved staple in Middle Eastern cuisine. It offers a comforting blend of earthy lentils, aromatic spices, and a bright finish of lemon and fresh herbs. Perfect for a nourishing meal on its own or as a starter, Adas is a healthy and satisfying dish for any time of year.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery and saute for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Do not brown them.

instructions.title: Add Garlic and Spices
instructions.text: Add the minced garlic to the pot and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the ground cumin, ground coriander, and turmeric powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and release their aroma.

instructions.title: Combine with Lentils and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, stirring to combine them with the vegetables and spices. Pour in the vegetable broth or water, ensuring all ingredients are submerged. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the soup simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking to the bottom of the pot.

instructions.title: Season and Finish
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in the fresh lemon juice. For a smoother soup, you can use an immersion blender to blend a portion or all of the soup to your desired consistency. Alternatively, mash some of the lentils with the back of a spoon.

instructions.title: Serve Adas Soup
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley. Serve immediately with warm pita bread, crusty bread, or a side salad. Enjoy this comforting and flavorful Middle Eastern classic.

tips: For extra depth of flavor, saute a small amount of vermicelli pasta in olive oil until golden brown before adding it to the soup along with the lentils and broth.
Adjust the amount of lemon juice to your preference; a fresh squeeze of lemon right before serving truly brightens the soup.
Store leftover Adas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It thickens as it cools, so you may need to add a splash of water or broth when reheating.
article:
Discover the heartwarming embrace of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known affectionately across the Middle East as Adas. This simple yet profoundly flavorful soup is a staple in Lebanese households, a culinary symbol of comfort, nutrition, and tradition. Whether you're seeking a quick weeknight meal, a nutritious lunch, or a soothing remedy for a chilly evening, Adas delivers a rich, earthy taste that satisfies the soul. It's a testament to how humble ingredients can transform into something truly extraordinary, embodying the essence of Middle Eastern hospitality and wholesome cooking.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas)?

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is a vibrant, nourishing soup made primarily from red lentils, often seasoned with aromatic vegetables like onions and garlic, and brightened with a generous squeeze of lemon juice. The word "Adas" itself means lentils in Arabic, highlighting the star ingredient of this beloved dish. Unlike some more elaborate Middle Eastern soups and stews, Adas is celebrated for its simplicity and speed of preparation. It’s naturally vegetarian and vegan-friendly, making it a popular choice for families and those observing dietary restrictions.

This soup's roots run deep in Lebanese and wider Middle Eastern cuisine, where lentils have been a dietary cornerstone for millennia. Historically, lentils provided essential protein and nutrients, especially during leaner times or for those who couldn't afford meat. Today, Adas remains a cherished part of the culinary landscape, served in homes, restaurants, and often as a comforting dish during the holy month of Ramadan. Its characteristic creamy texture (achieved either through natural breakdown of the lentils or a quick blend) and the refreshing tang of lemon make it instantly recognizable and utterly delicious.

## Why You'll Love This Adas Soup Recipe

There are countless reasons why Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas has captivated palates for generations, and why this particular recipe will become a treasured addition to your culinary repertoire:

*   **Incredibly Nutritious:** Red lentils are packed with protein, fiber, iron, and essential vitamins, making this soup a powerhouse of health benefits. It's a fantastic way to boost your daily nutrient intake.
*   **Quick & Easy to Make:** With minimal chopping and a relatively short cooking time, Adas is perfect for busy weeknights. Most of the cooking is hands-off simmering.
*   **Budget-Friendly:** Lentils are one of the most economical pantry staples, making this a very cost-effective meal that doesn't skimp on flavor or satisfaction.
*   **Naturally Vegan & Gluten-Free:** This recipe caters to a wide range of dietary needs without needing any modifications, making it an inclusive dish for almost any gathering.
*   **Deeply Comforting:** The warm, hearty texture and savory flavors make Adas the ultimate comfort food, perfect for soothing cold days or simply unwinding after a long day.
*   **Versatile:** While delicious on its own, Adas serves as an excellent canvas for various additions, allowing you to customize it to your liking.

## Ingredients You'll Need

Creating a truly authentic and flavorful Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas requires a handful of simple, wholesome ingredients:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Ensure they are rinsed thoroughly.
*   **Olive Oil:** A generous amount for sautéing and drizzling, adding richness and a characteristic Mediterranean flavor.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic base that builds a foundational layer of flavor.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** For the liquid base. Broth adds more depth, but water works perfectly well.
*   **Cumin:** Essential for that earthy, warm, and distinctly Middle Eastern flavor profile.
*   **Coriander:** Complements the cumin beautifully, adding a hint of citrusy, savory notes.
*   **Turmeric:** For a touch of color and its subtle earthy flavor and health benefits.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste, enhancing all the other flavors.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice:** Crucial for brightening the soup and cutting through the richness. Don't skip this!
*   **Fresh Mint or Parsley (optional, for garnish):** Adds a burst of freshness and visual appeal.

## How to Make Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas (Step-by-Step)

Follow these simple steps to create a delicious pot of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas:

1.  **Rinse Lentils:** Place red lentils in a fine-mesh sieve and rinse under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any dust or debris.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Add Spices:** Stir in cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 30 seconds to 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant. This helps to bloom the spices and deepen their flavor.
4.  **Combine & Simmer:** Add the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth (or water) to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend (Optional):** For a smoother soup, carefully use an immersion blender directly in the pot, or transfer portions to a regular blender (venting the lid to release steam) and blend until desired consistency is reached. You can blend a portion or all of it.
6.  **Finish with Lemon:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the fresh lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice to your preference.
7.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Garnish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and fresh mint or parsley, if desired.

## Pro Tips for the Best Adas Soup

Elevate your Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas with these expert tips:

*   **Don't Skimp on Lemon:** Lemon juice is absolutely vital for balancing the earthy flavors of the lentils. Add it at the end to preserve its bright acidity.
*   **Fresh Herbs are Key:** While optional, a sprinkle of fresh mint or parsley before serving adds a wonderful aromatic lift and visual appeal.
*   **Toasting Spices:** Briefly cooking the spices in oil before adding liquid (as in step 3) enhances their fragrance and deepens their flavor profile.
*   **Quality Olive Oil:** Use good quality extra virgin olive oil, especially for the final drizzle. It makes a noticeable difference in taste.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** If you prefer a thinner soup, add a little more broth or water. For a thicker consistency, simmer uncovered for a few extra minutes or blend more thoroughly.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your soup before serving and adjust salt, pepper, and especially lemon juice to your personal preference.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is a wonderfully versatile dish that can be enjoyed in many ways:

*   **With Pita Bread:** A classic pairing. Warm pita bread is perfect for scooping up the hearty soup.
*   **Alongside a Simple Salad:** A fresh green salad with a lemon-tahini dressing provides a refreshing contrast.
*   **As a Light Meal:** It's filling enough to be a meal on its own, especially when served with a piece of crusty bread.
*   **With Rice:** Some prefer to serve Adas over a small portion of plain white rice for an even heartier meal.
*   **Add a Swirl:** A swirl of plain yogurt (dairy or non-dairy) can add a creamy tang, though traditionally it's served vegan.

## Variations & Substitutions

Feel free to get creative with your Adas!

*   **Add Vegetables:** Stir in chopped carrots, celery, or spinach during the last 10 minutes of simmering for extra nutrients and texture.
*   **Spice It Up:** A pinch of red pepper flakes or a dash of Aleppo pepper can add a subtle kick.
*   **Herb Variations:** Experiment with dried mint, or a mix of fresh herbs like cilantro.
*   **Garnish Options:** Toasted pine nuts, a sprinkle of sumac, or crispy fried onions can add extra texture and flavor.
*   **Make it Thicker:** For a stew-like consistency, reduce the liquid slightly or blend more of the lentils.
*   **Different Lentils:** While red lentils are traditional, you could try green or brown lentils, though the cooking time and final texture will differ (they won't break down as much).

## Storage & Reheating Tips

Adas is fantastic for meal prep!

*   **Storage:** Store leftover Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
*   **Freezing:** This soup freezes beautifully. Allow it to cool completely, then transfer to freezer-safe containers or bags. It can be frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.
*   **Reheating:** Reheat gently on the stovetop over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until warmed through. You may need to add a splash of water or broth to adjust the consistency, as it can thicken in the fridge. Always taste and adjust seasonings, especially lemon juice, after reheating.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Q: Is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas always vegan?**
A: Yes, traditional Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is naturally vegan, made with plant-based ingredients like lentils, vegetables, olive oil, and spices.

**Q: Can I make this soup in an Instant Pot or slow cooker?**
A: Absolutely! For an Instant Pot, sauté the aromatics, add other ingredients, and cook on high pressure for 10-12 minutes with a natural release. For a slow cooker, sauté aromatics separately, then combine all ingredients in the slow cooker and cook on low for 6-8 hours or high for 3-4 hours.

**Q: What kind of red lentils should I use?**
A: Look for split red lentils, which cook quickly and break down easily, giving the soup its characteristic creamy texture. Whole red lentils will also work but may take a little longer to cook and won't be as smooth.

**Q: Can I add meat to this soup?**
A: While traditionally vegan, you could add cooked ground lamb or beef to the soup for a heartier, non-vegan version. Sauté it with the onions and garlic.

**Q: My soup is too thick/thin. How can I fix it?**
A: If it's too thick, add more vegetable broth or water until you reach your desired consistency. If it's too thin, simmer it uncovered for a bit longer to allow some liquid to evaporate, or blend a portion of the soup to thicken it.
